images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of PixelMatte. (a) Latent diffusion matting predicts the matte as a latent code between a frozen VAE encoder and a frozen VAE decoder. (b) PixelMatte embeds the noisy matte, the image and the trimap as pixel tokens on a shared grid and predicts the matte in a single forward pass without a VAE. LayerShift acts inside the backbone, and the High-Pass Refiner refines the predicted matte.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on P3M-500-NP, AM-2K, AIM-500 and RM-2K. From left to right: input image, trimap, ViTMatte-B, RenderMatte, PixelMatte and the ground-truth alpha matte. Each row shows a zoomed region.

Figure 5:Visualization of opacity and boundary calibration. Each row compares the alpha mattes before and after a calibration module against the ground truth. Error maps show prediction minus ground truth, while correction maps show the matte after minus before, using a shared color scale. LayerShift adjusts regional opacity levels (top), whereas the High-Pass Refiner concentrates its corrections around fine boundaries (middle and bottom).
